story.title: Winding World
story.premise: The Winding World is soft. Its islands stretch, its causeways bend, its reefs drift with the tides — and none of that matters, because what the world truly keeps is its holes: the rings, loops and hollows that let every route wind away and come home. Count Null sees those holes as flaws. Crowned with the Null Crown, he begins 'simplifying' the provinces one by one, collapsing ring to ball to point. His machines don't preserve shape; they erase it. Gyroid, a courier born of the surfaces, survives the first collapse on Retract Reef with nothing but an anchor spool and a lash. With the engineer Emmy Boundary, Gyroid sets out to undo the damage — and keeps running into the same problem: every time Gyroid saves a place, Null claims it was 'really' simpler all along, and Gyroid has no way to prove him wrong. Each world gives Gyroid a sharper way of seeing holes, and each one Null tries to slip past.
story.tone: Wonder-filled mathematical adventure; tactile, luminous, gently punning, with threatening geometric machinery and hopeful reconstruction.
story.teaching_spine: Five worlds follow Hatcher's five chapters, one key concept per level. Each world opens with Count Null exploiting what the player's current tool cannot see — a ring 'is' a point (World 0), the sphere 'is' a point because loops shrink (World 1), the torus 'is' S¹∨S¹∨S² because homology matches (World 2), S³ → S² 'must' be trivial (World 3), homotopy groups 'are' the whole space (World 4) — and the next world's invariant refutes him.
story.logline: When Count Null starts erasing the holes that hold the Winding World together, a courier who can't prove anything yet has to learn — world by world — the tools that show a hole is really there.
story.setting: The Winding World is five provinces strung along the Winding Way, a great causeway that loops through all of them. Null's first collapse severed the Way. Each province is an open overworld: Gyroid lands on its shore, roams between its sites (each a level), and finds paths blocked by gates that only earlier tools can open. Clearing a province's castle re-knits the Way to the next province, which is how Gyroid travels deeper — and how earlier lessons keep coming back. The provinces, in order: Retract Reef (walkways and forges; what 'same shape' means), Bouquet Bastion (loop districts and glass sheet-worlds; loops), Chain Delta (wetlands of oriented triangles; cycles and boundaries), the Cup Product Gardens (signal gardens; classes that multiply), and the Postnikov Spire (a tower of unfolding rooms; higher homotopy), where the Null Crown waits.

characters.arc: Courier → keeper. Gyroid starts out fixing things by feel: if it bends without tearing, it's fine. In World 0 that is enough to save places but not to win arguments — Null's claim that a ring is just a point goes unanswered. World by world Gyroid learns to prove, not just do: winding numbers, cycles, cup products, homotopy groups. By the end Gyroid is the one who can say exactly what a place is, and why it can't be simplified.

Mentor with a debt. Emmy guides Gyroid with hands-on examples and refuses to just hand over answers. In World 0's Skeleton Foundry it comes out that she built the first cell presses there — the machines Null's engineers later bent into collapse engines; she believed simplifying routes would help the couriers. Her arc is making that right: each world she builds Gyroid a better instrument, and at the Spire she is the one who refuses to finish Null's last collapse drive.

Null's route marshal, obsessed with order: his ribbon patrols run a, b, a⁻¹, b⁻¹ and never commute. Defeated at his Keep in World 1 when Gyroid shows his patrol loop can't be undone in the figure-eight. Returns in World 3 in disguise, running a counterfeit station that matches the torus group for group — unmasked by a cup product. In the ending he takes up the job he was always good at: keeping the order of the restored routes, without erasing any.

Not a monster but a perfectionist. Null believes complexity is suffering and that a point, having nothing to lose, is the most perfect place there is. His tactic is always the same: find what Gyroid's current tool can't see, and claim the difference isn't real. His defeat isn't destruction. At the top of the Spire, with the Crown unwound, Gyroid hands him the first loop of the restored ring island — a loop he can carry but never shrink. He doesn't drop it.

world_arcs.title: Retract Reef — What counts as the same?
world_arcs.opening: After the first collapse, Gyroid washes up at the Landing Pier; the walkway's amber spine is the only thing still standing. Emmy finds him and explains: thick walkways can be shrunk onto their spines without losing anything that matters.
world_arcs.journey: Gyroid learns to deform without tearing (0-1, 0-2), discovers that very different-looking reefs can be the same shape (0-3), then crosses the Mirror Gate into the Skeleton Foundry, where places are built cell by cell (0-4 to 0-6). Emmy's past with the Foundry comes out.
world_arcs.castle: At the Hollow Throne Gyroid exposes Null's fake simplifications as torn or illegal — but when Null insists a ring is secretly a point, Gyroid has no proof. Null escapes along the broken Way.
world_arcs.turn: Gyroid needs an invariant: a way to show a hole is really there.

world_arcs.title: Bouquet Bastion — Loops
world_arcs.opening: Two loop districts meet at a single beacon; the Commutator's ribbon patrols keep travel order.
world_arcs.journey: Gyroid learns to treat loops as moves you can combine and undo, and to count how many times a loop winds (1-3) — which finally refutes the World 0 claim: a ring isn't a point, its loop winds once (1-4). Then free words, gluing, and the glass sheet-worlds of covering spaces.
world_arcs.castle: At the Commutator's Keep, his patrol aba⁻¹b⁻¹ is caught: it can't be undone in the figure-eight (a cover proves it), though it dies on the torus.
world_arcs.turn: Null retreats to a sphere, where every loop shrinks. Loops are blind there.

world_arcs.title: Chain Delta — Cycles remember what loops forget
world_arcs.opening: On the sphere, Null shows every loop shrinking to nothing. Emmy: stop counting paths, start counting what they enclose.
world_arcs.journey: Oriented triangles, boundaries that cancel, cycles that survive. Homology hears the sphere's hollow that loops couldn't feel (2-6), and makes the Commutator's old trick vanish (2-10).
world_arcs.castle: Null's retractor tries to squash a ball onto its boundary; it can't work (Brouwer, one dimension up).
world_arcs.turn: Null's new claim: the torus and a wedge of two circles and a sphere are the same place — their homology matches.

world_arcs.title: Cup Product Gardens — Classes that multiply
world_arcs.opening: Gardens where signals read chains backwards. A station that looks exactly like the torus, group for group.
world_arcs.journey: Cochains, then the cup product: classes can be multiplied, and the product tells places apart that homology can't (3-4). Orientation, and duality.
world_arcs.castle: The counterfeit station falls: its cup products vanish where the torus's don't. The Commutator is unmasked.
world_arcs.turn: Null climbs his tower into higher homotopy, claiming no map from S³ to S² can be essential.

world_arcs.title: Postnikov Spire — Twists
world_arcs.opening: Rooms that unfold into higher dimensions; the Null Crown at the top.
world_arcs.journey: Higher homotopy groups, Freudenthal, Hurewicz — and the Hopf fibration, which refutes Null's World 3 claim (4-7). Then the tower itself: Eilenberg–MacLane floors, k-invariant twists, obstructions.
world_arcs.castle: Null's last claim: give him the homotopy groups and he'll rebuild any space; the twists don't matter. Gyroid rebuilds the Crown's tower stage by stage, installing the twists Null threw away.
world_arcs.turn: The collapse drive disconnects. The Way re-knits end to end.

story.ending: The ringed island from the opening rises back out of the sea, hole and all, and every province is restored without erasing a single hole. Null is left at the top of the empty Spire holding the island's first loop — the one thing he could never shrink. The Commutator walks the restored routes in their proper order. Emmy retires her presses. Gyroid goes back to running deliveries, but now as the keeper of the Way: the one who can tell anyone exactly what shape their home is. Final line, echoing the tagline: shape changed; topology didn't.
themes: Difference isn't damage: the holes are what make a place itself.
Doing versus proving: Gyroid can save a place long before he can prove it was worth saving; each world closes that gap.
Every tool has a blind spot; the next one sees what it missed.

locations.name: Retract Reef
locations.description: Turquoise thickened graph walkways over a luminous sea. Amber spines remain fixed as their neighborhoods retract; cylinder workshops let players extend boundary motions continuously.

locations.name: Skeleton Foundry
locations.description: An open industrial valley of vertex furnaces, oriented edge cranes and disk presses. A torus gate displays its attaching polygon and glued form side by side; the approach network has a marked collapsible spanning tree.

locations.name: Bouquet Bastion
locations.description: Two unfilled loop districts meet at a single beacon. Red and violet causeways keep travel order visible; thickened open neighborhoods provide the connected overlap for the van Kampen construction.

locations.name: Sheetwater Viaduct
locations.description: A connected three-sheet cover of the bouquet, shown as layered glass routes with locally matched labeled ports. Sheet changes occur only by traversing lifted edges, never by jumping between visual layers.

locations.name: Chain Delta
locations.description: An annular wetland built from oriented triangular platforms, with a conspicuously absent central region. Signed face projections reveal interior-edge cancellation while the missing center preserves a nonbounding cycle.

locations.name: Degree Dynamo
locations.description: A spherical power station with overlapping polar maintenance patches and an equatorial belt. Map projectors show signed sphere wraps; a transparent ball chamber exposes the false boundary retractor's induced-map contradiction.

locations.name: Cup Product Gardens
locations.description: A toroidal signal garden beside a counterfeit wedge of two circles and a sphere. Ordered triangulations and cochain sensors let players distinguish the stations by cup products rather than silhouettes or homology groups alone.

locations.name: Poincaré Reach
locations.description: A closed toroidal province with primal and dual route networks, and a separate projective-plane annex displayed through a disk with antipodal boundary identifications. Orientation transport and coefficient switching reveal different fundamental-class rules.

locations.name: Freudenthal Ascent
locations.description: A vertical series of double-cone lifts and based-cube projection chambers. Dimension and connectivity controls expose suspension's valid range; higher-dimensional spaces are represented by manipulable finite diagrams and slices.

locations.name: Postnikov Spire
locations.description: Count Null's fortress of linked stages suspended above the provinces. Two authored simply connected Postnikov-stage consoles display finite cochain models, k-invariant couplings and obstruction witnesses; restored lifts lead to the Crown's collapse engine.

characters.name: Gyroid
characters.description: A curious surface-born courier whose sea-glass armor has the saddle-shaped passages of a gyroid minimal surface. Uses anchored deformations and constructive proofs rather than destructive force. Learns alongside the player; failed moves reveal a concrete continuity, boundary, or obstruction witness.

characters.description: Count Null's theatrical route marshal, wearing two loop-shaped pauldrons and wielding ordered ribbon patrols. characters.name: Count Null
characters.description: An austere sovereign who mistakes erasing structure for simplifying it. His collapse machinery can physically destroy holes but cannot make the resulting maps homotopy equivalences. Challenges the hero with false retractions, overextended theorems, and missing tower couplings; defeated by restored constructions and explicit obstruction witnesses.

worlds.title: Retract Reef
worlds.theme: Thick walkways over a luminous sea, built and rebuilt cell by cell. What does it mean for two shapes to be 'the same'?

null_claim.claim: A ring is just a point that hasn't been simplified yet.
null_claim.why_it_works_here: World 0 can show deformations that work, but has no invariant that proves one is impossible (Hatcher p. 3 defers this to Chapter 1).

levels.title: A Good Deformation
levels.concept: Deformation retraction: shrink X onto a subspace A by sliding points, with f₀ = identity, f₁(X) = A, A fixed throughout, and continuity in both point and time.
levels.goal: Save Retract Reef's walkways by shrinking each thick walkway onto an amber spine you draw through its beacons, sliding every point along a straight segment without leaving the reef, tearing, or moving the spine.
levels.teaches: Thick shapes shrink to thin spines by sliding points along segments at constant speed (Hatcher's thick-letter example). A valid deformation retraction starts at the identity, ends inside A, never moves A, and is continuous. Rings and two-holed disks shrink to loops and graphs, never (by sliding) to a point.

beats.teach: A straight walkway with a given spine: scrub time t from 0 to 1 and watch each point slide along its segment; the four rules light up.
beats.practice: A thick T: draw a spine through all three beacons and run the slide.
beats.twist: A thick O (ring): a short spine fails — points must cross the hole and fall into the sea, or neighbors tear apart. Only a loop around the hole works.
beats.master: A disk with two holes (Hatcher's figure): find a spine that holds; Emmy notes the book shows three different ones. Then spot Count Null's four forged 'retractions', each breaking one rule.

art.scene: Level 'A Good Deformation' on Retract Reef. A thick round basalt reef with two lagoon holes in it. Gyroid runs across it holding a thick glowing gold ring (the Spool), paying out a glowing gold thread behind him that loops around both lagoons, forming a figure-eight spine. Part of the reef is mid-collapse: the thick stone slabs slide smoothly inward toward the gold spine along faint glowing guide lines, shrinking onto it without cracking. A small dark-violet sphere creature and a dark-violet torus creature approach across the reef; a thin gold lasso arcs from Gyroid's hand toward the torus.

design.site: Retract Reef overworld: Landing Pier → the Walkway, the Fork, the O, Twin Lagoons → Null's Mirage at the broken causeway.
design.story: Morning after the collapse. Gyroid wakes at the Landing Pier; the walkway slabs are gone but the amber spines held. Emmy shows how a thick reef shrinks onto its spine without losing anything that matters. With four reefs saved, Null's Mirage stages four forged 'retractions'; naming the broken rule in each mends the causeway to Tidewarp Flats.
design.objective: Save the four reefs by shrinking each onto a spine through its beacons, then expose Null's four forgeries.
mechanics: Explore in third person (WASD); overhead follow camera; minimap from the World 0 map.
Fundamental Lash (click toward the mouse): spheres collapse in one lash, tori need two (one loop each).
Spool (2 / Q, click to start and stop): walk to lay spine thread on a reef.
Slide: the reef deformation-retracts onto the spine; Gyroid rides his own tile. Saved reefs regrow, healed.
The spine is valid when it is connected and every region of reef − spine touches exactly one shore; otherwise the failing region turns red with a diagnosis (leak / fenced patch / disconnected).
design.math_check: Deformation retraction of a planar region onto a drawn graph: valid iff the spine is connected and each complementary region is a collar on a single boundary curve; the slide follows the gradient of a harmonic function in each collar (continuous by construction).

stages.name: The Walkway
stages.description: Clear two spheres; the spine is given; watch the slide and the five rules turn green.

stages.name: The Fork
stages.description: A thick T: spool a spine through three beacons.

stages.name: The O
stages.description: First torus. A short spine leaks across the ring; only a loop around the hole holds.

stages.name: Twin Lagoons
stages.description: A disk with two holes: figure-eight, theta or barbell spines all work (Hatcher's three).

stages.name: Null's Mirage
stages.description: Four forgeries, each breaking one rule; name the rule. Wins mend the broken causeway.

enemies.name: Sphere spawn
enemies.description: One lash; loops slide off a sphere, so it collapses to a point.

enemies.name: Torus spawn
enemies.description: Two lashes: the first lights a loop around its tube, the second a loop through its hole.

design.tools: Uses the Lash; unlocks the Spool (anchor_spool).
design.music: The Retract Reef theme: 92 bpm D dorian chiptune — pads, echoing pulse arpeggio, triangle bass, sine lead on the second phrase.
design.visuals: Basalt reefs on a dark luminous sea, gold spines and beacons, violet spawn; saved reefs warm to a pale gold-grey.

levels.title: Bend, Don't Break
levels.concept: Homotopy of maps in general; homotopy rel A; retraction vs. deformation retraction (every space retracts to a point, but not every space deformation retracts to one).
levels.goal: Morph one map into another through a continuous family; keep a marked subspace still (rel A); catch the constant-map 'retraction' that isn't a deformation.

art.scene: Level 'Bend, Don't Break' on Tidewarp Flats: wide wet basalt tidal flats with shallow glowing water. A single glowing gold ribbon path runs across the flats between two fixed glowing stone posts at its ends. Around it, several faint translucent gold copies of the SAME ribbon show it at earlier moments — first straight, then gently bowed, then a smooth S-curve — like a long-exposure photograph of one ribbon slowly bending. The ribbon is the only thing shown in multiple copies; Gyroid appears exactly once. A third stone post in the middle of the ribbon glows steadily and every copy passes through it — that point never moves. Gyroid (one single figure) stands beside the ribbon, guiding it with his gold lasso. Off to one side, a violet counterfeit ribbon has visibly snapped in two, its broken ends sparking violet.

design.site: Tidewarp Flats — wide wet basalt flats east of the mended causeway, with tide pools and stone posts.
design.story: Past the mended causeway the tide reshapes every path on the flats each hour. Null's engineers 'help' by snapping paths straight to a single post. Gyroid learns that a homotopy is the whole continuous movie of maps — and that a snap is not a movie.
design.objective: Guide the tide: deform gold ribbon-paths into the shapes the shrines ask for, keeping the marked posts fixed, without crossing open water.
mechanics: Ribbons are maps from an interval into the flats. Gyroid grabs a ribbon point with the Spool and walks it; the ribbon bends continuously behind him (a homotopy, recorded as a ghost trail).
Posts pin points of a ribbon: a homotopy rel those posts never moves them.
Tide pools are holes in the flats: a ribbon can't pass through water, so some targets can only be reached by going around.
Tide Glass (new): scrub a recorded deformation backwards and forwards in time — every frame must connect to the next.
Null's Snap: a ‘deformation’ that jumps; the player finds the frame where it tears.
design.math_check: Path homotopy in a planar region with holes, rel endpoints; continuity in time (consecutive frames are close); retraction (a single map) versus deformation retraction (a continuous family).

stages.name: Tide Line
stages.description: The tide bends a ribbon on its own; scrub the Tide Glass and watch a homotopy as a movie of maps.

stages.name: Hold the Posts
stages.description: Walk a ribbon into the shrine's target shape with both end posts fixed — a homotopy rel endpoints.

stages.name: The Pools
stages.description: Two targets on opposite sides of a tide pool: one is reachable by sliding around the pool, the other isn't by any slide Gyroid can find. Emmy: proving it's impossible needs a tool from the next world.

stages.name: Null's Snap
stages.description: Null retracts the whole flats onto one post in a single snap. Every space retracts to a point; find the frame where his ‘deformation’ tears.

enemies.name: Snapper
enemies.description: New: a violet crab that clips ribbons. A clipped ribbon is discontinuous and must be re-tied before the shrine accepts it. One lash.

enemies.name: Sphere and torus spawn
enemies.description: As in 0-1, now drifting with the tide.

design.tools: Uses the Lash and Spool; unlocks the Tide Glass (scrub time).
design.music: Variation on the reef theme: slower (80 bpm), tidal swells on the pad, a ticking clock-like pluck when the Tide Glass is out.
design.visuals: Mirror-wet basalt flats at low tide, stone posts, glowing gold ribbons with translucent ghost copies; violet sparks where a snap tears.

levels.title: Same Shape, Different Look
levels.concept: Homotopy equivalence (fg ≃ 1, gf ≃ 1), contractible spaces, mapping cylinders.
levels.goal: Show two walkway networks with different spines from 0-1 are 'the same shape' by building maps both ways and deforming the round trips back to the identity.

art.scene: Level 'Same Shape, Different Look' at Mirror Shoals. A calm glassy channel of water acts as a mirror between two thick basalt reefs. LEFT reef: a thick figure-eight — exactly two round lagoon holes side by side, the two loops touching at a single central point. RIGHT reef: a thick theta — one oval ring with exactly ONE straight bar across its middle, so it has exactly TWO half-oval lagoon holes (not four; no cross, no second bar). Each reef has exactly two holes. Glowing gold threads stretch across the channel from points of one reef to points of the other in both directions. Gyroid stands on a slender stone bridge over the mirror channel, looking from one reef to the other. In the background, a solid round reef with no holes gently shrinks toward a single glowing point.

design.site: Mirror Shoals — five reefs on either side of a glassy, star-reflecting channel: Solid Shoal, Ring Reef, Twin Mirror, the Dumbbell, and the reef before the Mirror Gate to the Skeleton Foundry.
design.story: The figure-eight and the theta both came from Twin Lagoons, yet they look nothing alike. Emmy shows how to prove two places are 'the same shape': maps both ways whose round trips slide home. The Mirror Gate opens only for someone who can do it — and Emmy seems to know what's behind it.
design.objective: Prove reefs are the same shape: shrink loops, slide reefs onto spines (0-1's deformation retraction), and show one reef slides onto two different spines — then open the Mirror Gate.
mechanics: Loops on stakes (0-2's Spool): unhook every stake and a loop on solid ground shrinks to its post; around a hole it catches.
Point spine: a one-point spine slides a solid reef onto a point — contractible (homotopy equivalent to a point).

Two spines, one reef: the same two-hole reef deformation retracts onto a figure-eight and onto a theta, so they are homotopy equivalent (Hatcher, Corollary 0.21: both are deformation retracts of one space).
One loop per hole: a ring spine on a two-hole reef leaks; adding a second loop and a bar (a barbell) works.
Mirror spawn: each has an intangible reflection across its reef's mirror line; only the solid one can be lashed.
The lesson shows explicit maps f : eight → theta and g : theta → eight (collapse the bar) whose round trips slide home.
design.math_check: Homotopy equivalence (fg ≃ 1, gf ≃ 1) and contractibility (Hatcher pp. 3–4), proved in play via deformation retractions checked by the 0-1 slide engine; X ≃ Y iff both are deformation retracts of some Z (Corollary 0.21, p. 16). Flag: that the ring is not contractible is left unproved until World 1.

stages.name: Solid Shoal
stages.description: Unhook a loop: it shrinks to its post. Then a one-point spine slides the whole reef onto a point — contractible.

stages.name: Ring Reef
stages.description: Its loop catches on the hole; Emmy flags that proving it can't shrink needs World 1.

stages.name: Twin Mirror
stages.description: Slide one two-hole reef onto a figure-eight, let it regrow, then onto a theta: the two spines are the same shape.

stages.name: Dumbbell
stages.description: Null's ring spine leaks (a hole without a loop); a barbell spine works.

stages.name: The Mirror Gate
stages.description: Any valid spine on an odd two-hole reef; the gate lights figure-eight, theta and barbell, leaves the ring dark, and opens onto the Foundry.

enemies.name: Mirror spawn
enemies.description: New: a faceted mirror-crystal creature with an intangible, flickering reflection across its reef's mirror line; lash the solid one. One lash.

enemies.name: Sphere and torus spawn
enemies.description: One and two lashes.

design.tools: Uses the Lash and Spool (spines and loops).
design.music: Mirror Shoals theme: 72 bpm E lydian celesta bells over a slow pad; every two-bar motif is answered by its mirror image (inverted).
design.visuals: A still mirror channel reflecting stars; two thick basalt reefs; gold threads arcing between them; a tall mirrored gate with forge-light behind it.

levels.title: Some Assembly Required
levels.concept: CW complexes: attach n-cells along their boundaries to the (n−1)-skeleton; S², torus, RP² from cells; Euler characteristic as a cell count.
levels.goal: Forge S², the torus (aba⁻¹b⁻¹) and RP² from vertices, edges and disks, previewing each attaching map before gluing.

art.scene: Level 'Some Assembly Required' inside the Assembly Hall of the Skeleton Foundry, a vast basalt industrial hall with forges. Glowing vertex furnaces emit single bright points of light; mechanical crane arms lay curved glowing edges between points; a great press lowers a translucent glowing disk onto a closed loop. In the center, a flat glowing square sheet with arrow-marked edges is folding in mid-air: one pair of opposite edges has curled together into a tube and the tube is bending around to close into a torus. Gyroid stands at a forge wearing a brass-and-indigo gauntlet (the Cell-Smith) that levitates a point, a curved edge and a translucent triangle above his palm.

design.site: The Skeleton Foundry's Assembly Hall — four forge stations (round basalt platforms with a furnace hub and petal tracks) under a press gantry, and the forge door to the Cone Zone.
design.story: Through the Mirror Gate, Emmy's secret comes out: she built the Foundry's cell presses, and Null's engineers turned them into collapse engines. She gives Gyroid the Cell-Smith so they can build places back — cell by cell.
design.objective: Forge cell complexes at four presses — the sphere (twice), the torus, the projective plane and the Klein bottle — and open the forge door with χ.
mechanics: Cell-Smith (new): click the furnace hub to forge the point (the one 0-cell).
Walk a petal track out from the hub and back: an edge (a 1-cell), a loop at the point, arrow in the direction walked, lettered a, b.
Walk a word along the edges (forward = a, against the arrow = a⁻¹), then click the hub: the press glues a disk (a 2-cell) along that loop.
The press's hologram folds the flat cell into the space it makes; a wrong word builds something else, shown and explained, then let go.
χ = points − edges + disks, counted live on the blueprint card.
Unglues tear forged edges; re-walk a torn track to re-forge it.
design.math_check: Cell complexes built skeleton by skeleton (Hatcher pp. 5–8); one-vertex structures: S² = e⁰ ∪ e² and also e⁰ ∪ e¹ ∪ 2e²; T² along a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹; RP² along a a; Klein bottle along a b a⁻¹ b; χ as even minus odd cells (Example 0.2). Flag: that χ depends only on the space is Theorem 2.44 (Chapter 2) — stated, not proved here. Also: with one vertex, a disk on a a⁻¹ is a sphere with two points glued (χ = 1), and the game says so.

stages.name: The Sphere Press
stages.description: Point + a disk with its rim crushed to it: a sphere. Again as one edge + two hemispheres: same χ = 2.

stages.name: Twin Loops
stages.description: Edges a, b; a disk along a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹: the torus folds (roll, then bend). χ = 0.

stages.name: One Loop
stages.description: A disk along a just fills the loop (a disk); along a a it's the projective plane, which crosses itself in 3D.

stages.name: The Blueprint Wall
stages.description: a b a⁻¹ b under an Unglue wave: the Klein bottle; then answer χ = 0 to open the forge door.

enemies.name: Unglue
enemies.description: New: a violet seam-ripper that tears forged edges loose; re-walk the track to re-forge. One lash.

enemies.name: Sphere and torus spawn
enemies.description: One and two lashes.

design.music: Forge theme: 100 bpm C minor — anvil strikes on the off-beats, square bass and brass, bellows swells, the reef melody in minor.
design.visuals: Basalt forge hall, furnaces glowing amber, cranes laying curved glowing edges, a square sheet folding into a torus mid-air; Gyroid's brass-and-indigo gauntlet.

levels.title: Cone Zone
levels.concept: Operations on spaces: products, quotients, cones, suspensions, wedges, joins — and the cells each inherits or adds.
levels.goal: Turn spaces into their cone, suspension and wedge with the Cell-Smith; build the torus again as S¹ × S¹ and match it to your 0-4 torus.

art.scene: Level 'Cone Zone' on a basalt terrace of the Skeleton Foundry with glowing workstations, each showing an operation on a shape: a glowing ring with straight gold lines rising from it to a single apex point, forming a cone; a glowing ring with lines to two apex points, one above and one below, forming a double cone (a suspension); two glowing loops joined at a single shared point (a wedge); and a small circle being swept around a larger circle so its path forms a torus. Gyroid walks between the stations holding a sling of gold cord.

design.site: Cone Zone — a terrace of workstations on the Foundry cliff.
design.story: Null's engineers are 'fixing' ring islands by coning them off: joining every point of a ring to one tip, which fills the hole. Gyroid learns the operations on spaces — cone, suspension, wedge, product, quotient — so a plugged hole can't fool him.
design.objective: Stop the coning crews and use the stations to build target spaces from simpler ones.
mechanics: Operation stations: feed a space in, choose cone, suspension, wedge or product, and get the new space (with its cells added).
Recipe puzzles: reach a target space by a chain of operations (circle → suspension → sphere; circle × circle → torus; circle ∨ circle → figure-eight).
Quotients: collapse a subspace to a point; collapsing something contractible keeps the shape, collapsing a loop doesn't.
Spot the plug: a coned ring is a disk — contractible — even if it still looks like a ring from the side.
design.math_check: Cones are contractible; suspension of Sⁿ is Sⁿ⁺¹; products and wedges add cells predictably; collapsing a contractible subcomplex preserves homotopy type.

stages.name: The Cone
stages.description: Watch a crew cone a ring: the hole fills. Any cone shrinks to its tip.

stages.name: Two Tips
stages.description: Suspend two points: a circle. Suspend a circle: a sphere.

stages.name: Wedge and Product
stages.description: Build the figure-eight as a wedge and the torus as circle × circle; compare it with the torus from the Assembly Hall by counting cells.

stages.name: Recipes
stages.description: Chain operations to match three targets while coning crews try to plug your inputs.

enemies.name: Coner
enemies.description: New: a violet engineer drone that beams a cone onto a ring; lash it before the beam finishes or the ring is plugged. Two lashes.

enemies.name: Sphere spawn
enemies.description: One lash.

design.tools: Uses the Cell-Smith; unlocks the Suspension Sling (suspension_sling).

design.visuals: Terraced basalt stations under moonlight, glowing gold cones and double cones, a small circle sweeping a torus; violet drones with cone beams.
design.movie: level-0-5-intro “Null's Plugs” and the lesson level-0-5-lesson “New Spaces from Old”.

levels.title: Timber!
levels.concept: Collapsing a contractible subcomplex preserves homotopy type; collapse a spanning tree to turn any connected graph into a bouquet of circles; χ distinguishes bouquets.
levels.goal: Collapse only edges with distinct endpoints until each network is a bouquet; use Chi Euler's count to tell bouquets apart.

art.scene: Level 'Timber!' at the Timber Yard of the Skeleton Foundry: a network of narrow basalt walkways forming a graph of nodes and edges over the sea. A tree of edges is highlighted in glowing amber and is visibly collapsing — those walkways fold and shrink toward a single central node like timber being felled — while the remaining edges stay as loops, leaving a bouquet of several loops (petals) radiating from one central glowing node. Gyroid stands at the central node with his gold lasso. Emmy Boundary (older engineer, dark skin, silver curly hair, amber goggles, indigo patchwork coat of triangles) watches from a platform with a glowing triangular cell in her hand.

design.site: Timber Yard — a tangled network of narrow walkways over the sea at the Foundry's edge; the unbuilt bridge to the Hollow Throne starts here.
design.story: The yard's walkways have grown into a tangle. Felling a tree of walkways keeps the shape; felling a loop erases a hole — which is exactly what Null's spawn do. Counting platforms minus walkways tells bouquets apart. With the yard cleared, Gyroid forges the bridge to the Throne.
design.objective: Collapse each tangle to a bouquet of loops without killing a loop, and read its petal count from χ.
mechanics: Mark a tree with the Spool: amber walkways that reach every platform without closing a loop.
Fell: tree walkways fold toward one platform; the rest become petals of a bouquet.
Loop guard: trying to fell a walkway whose ends are the same platform is refused (it would erase a hole).
Census: χ = platforms − walkways never changes when a tree is felled; petals = 1 − χ.
Bridge: after the census, forge the Throne bridge's cells with the Cell-Smith.
design.math_check: Collapsing a contractible subcomplex (a tree) is a homotopy equivalence; every connected graph is ≃ a wedge of 1 − χ circles.

stages.name: One Edge
stages.description: Shrink a single walkway between two platforms: nothing is lost.

stages.name: Spanning Tree
stages.description: Mark a tree that touches every platform; fell it; count the petals.

stages.name: The Wrong Cut
stages.description: Loop-biter spawn collapse a petal; stop them, and see why a loop can't be felled.

stages.name: Census
stages.description: Three tangles that look different: fell all three and sort them by χ.

enemies.name: Loop-biter

enemies.name: Unglue

design.tools: Uses the Spool and Cell-Smith.

design.visuals: A web of narrow basalt walkways, a highlighted amber tree folding inward, petals of a bouquet around one glowing node; the black spire across the water.

levels.title: Extension Cord
levels.concept: Bonus: the homotopy extension property; every CW pair has it.
levels.goal: Extend a prescribed motion of the boundary across a cylinder, cell by cell, without changing the start.

art.scene: Bonus level 'Extension Cord' at Cylinder Works: inside a tall basalt workshop stands a huge translucent glowing cylinder. A pattern of gold light is fixed on its bottom face, and a band of moving gold light travels up one side; inside, the gold light is filling the cylinder's interior cell by cell, extending the motion upward through the whole volume. Gyroid stands on a gantry beside the cylinder, adjusting the flow with his gold lasso.

design.site: Cylinder Works — a sealed workshop off the Assembly Hall holding a huge translucent cylinder.
design.story: Emmy's first machine. If you already know how the edge of a piece moves, can you extend that motion over the whole piece without changing where it starts? For anything built from cells, yes — one cell at a time.
design.objective: Fill the cylinder's interior with a motion that matches the given floor and side band, cell by cell.
mechanics: The floor shows the starting map; a band on the side shows the prescribed motion of a subcomplex.
Extend cell by cell with the Cell-Smith, in order of dimension: points, then edges, then disks.
A cell can be filled only once the motion on its boundary is already decided.
design.math_check: The homotopy extension property for CW pairs: X×{0} ∪ A×I is a retract of X×I, built cell by cell.

stages.name: Full Cylinder
stages.description: Fill the whole interior.

castle.outcome: Gyroid exposes three of Null's 'simplifications' as torn or illegal, but cannot refute his claim that a ring is secretly a point. Null escapes. The player now needs an invariant.

design.site: The Hollow Throne — Null's black-glass spire in the northwest, reached over the bridge forged at the Timber Yard.
design.story: Gyroid climbs to Null's throne room, where the Null Crown hangs over a floor of shifting reef. Null tests everything World 0 taught: fake deformations, illegal collapses, false equivalences. Gyroid beats every forgery — but when Null insists a ring is secretly a point, Gyroid has no proof. Null laughs and escapes along the broken Winding Way.
design.objective: Survive Null's three trials and expose every illegal simplification.

phases.name: Live forgeries
phases.description: Null's deformations play out on the arena floor. Lash the frame where a rule breaks (starts still, stays on the reef, ends on the spine, spine fixed, no tearing) to freeze it. Tests 0-1 and 0-2.

phases.description: Null collapses three walkway networks. Lash the beacons of illegal collapses (a loop felled, a hole coned) and spare the legal ones (a tree felled). Tests 0-5 and 0-6.

worlds.theme: Loop districts, ordered causeways and glass sheet-worlds. Loops are the weapon; the Commutator patrols.

levels.title: Fixed Endpoints
levels.concept: Paths and path homotopy with endpoints held fixed; straight-line homotopy; homotopy classes; concatenation is well defined on classes.

design.site: Endpoint Gardens — formal gardens of hedged lawns between gatehouses, just past Wayfall Landing.
design.story: Bouquet Bastion's couriers deliver along garden paths between gatehouses. Two routes count as 'the same delivery' if one can slide into the other while both ends stay at their gates. Gyroid learns to sort routes into classes — the first step toward counting holes.
design.objective: Sort the gardeners' routes into delivery classes and chain deliveries together.
mechanics: Routes are paths between two gatehouses. Gyroid walks a route with the Spool; the Tide Glass (0-2) slides it, ends held fixed.
Delivery ledger: routes that slide into each other land in the same class (path homotopy rel endpoints).
Open lawns are convex: any two routes slide straight into each other (the straight-line homotopy).
Hedge beds are holes: routes going around different sides of a hedge may not slide together.
Chaining: a route A→B followed by B→C is a route A→C; its class depends only on the classes of the pieces.
design.math_check: Path homotopy rel endpoints is an equivalence relation; straight-line homotopy in convex sets; concatenation is well defined on classes.

stages.name: Open Lawn
stages.description: Every route across a hedge-free lawn slides straight onto every other: one class.

stages.name: Hedges
stages.description: Sort six routes around a hedge bed into classes in the ledger.

stages.name: Faster Isn't Different
stages.description: Walk the same route at a different pace: same class (reparametrizing is a homotopy).

stages.name: Chained Deliveries
stages.description: Chain routes through three gatehouses; swapping a piece for another in its class never changes the chain's class.

levels.title: Loop de Loop
levels.concept: Based loops form the fundamental group: concatenation, constant loop, inverses; change of basepoint along a path.

design.site: Basepoint Beacon — the tall amber beacon where the Bastion's two loop districts meet.
design.story: At the beacon, routes that start and end at the same place become loops — and loops can be combined, undone and compared. Gyroid's Lash learns to close loops, turning every lap around the beacon into a move in a group.
design.objective: Learn the loop moves — combine, reverse, cancel — and carry loops to a new beacon.
mechanics: Loop Lash (upgrade): any route that leaves the beacon and returns is recorded as a loop token.
Combine: run one loop, then another (concatenation).
Reverse: run a loop backwards; a loop followed by its reverse slides down to standing still.
Associativity: (α then β) then γ slides into α then (β then γ).
Change of beacon: carry loops to a second beacon along a path h; every loop γ becomes h, γ, h reversed — nothing is gained or lost.
design.math_check: π₁(X, x₀): concatenation of based loops up to homotopy is a group (identity, inverses, associativity); a path h gives an isomorphism π₁(X,x₀) ≅ π₁(X,x₁).

stages.name: Home Base
stages.description: A loop must start and end at the beacon; the standing-still loop is the identity.

stages.name: There and Back
stages.description: Run a loop then its reverse; slide the result down to the identity.

stages.name: Brackets Don't Matter
stages.description: Three loops combined two ways slide into each other.

stages.name: A Second Beacon
stages.description: Carry the whole loop collection to a second beacon along a path and back.

enemies.name: Torus spawn
enemies.description: Two lashes, one loop each — now Gyroid can see the loops the lashes light.

enemies.name: Ribbon patrol (scout)

design.tools: Unlocks the Loop Lash upgrade.
design.music: The Bastion march over a bell that tolls once each time a loop closes at the beacon.
design.visuals: A towering amber beacon at the junction of two stone ring districts, gold loop trails circling out and back, a second smaller beacon down a causeway.

art.scene: Level 'Loop de Loop' at the Basepoint Beacon: a towering amber beacon stands where two great ring-shaped stone causeway districts meet (one with red lanterns, one with violet). Glowing gold loop trails leave the beacon and return, overlapping. Gyroid stands at the beacon's base, a gold lasso closing into a loop. Far down one causeway a second smaller beacon glows.

levels.title: Winding Road
levels.concept: π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ: lift loops to the helix ℝ → S¹; the lift's endpoint is the winding number, and homotopy cannot change it.

design.site: The Winding Road — a round island with a stone helix ramp spiralling up into the sky above it.
design.story: Above a ring-shaped island rises a helix: every lap around the ring below is a full turn up the ramp above. Gyroid's shadow climbs the helix as he runs, and the floor it ends on is a number no sliding can change. Loops on a circle are counted by integers.
design.objective: Use the helix to count how many times loops wind, and show that sliding never changes the count.
mechanics: Winding Cord (new): as Gyroid walks the ring, a shadow lift climbs the helix above; when the loop closes, the cord shows the floor reached — the winding number.
Tide Glass slides on the ring never change the floor (homotopy lifting).
Combining loops adds their floors; reversing a loop negates it.
Winders spin around pillars a set number of times; Gyroid unwinds one by running a loop with the opposite winding, then lashes it.
design.math_check: π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ via the covering ℝ → S¹ (the helix): unique path lifting, homotopy lifting, the endpoint of the lift is the winding number, concatenation ↦ addition.

stages.name: The Helix
stages.description: One lap around the ring = one floor up the helix.

stages.name: Sliding Doesn't Count
stages.description: Deform a loop wildly with the Tide Glass: the floor never changes.

stages.name: Unwind
stages.description: Winders: combine loops so the floors cancel (2 + (−2) = 0), then lash.

stages.name: The Number Line
stages.description: Gates demand exact winding numbers built from given loops; every integer is reachable, and nothing else.

design.visuals: A round stone island, a spectacular helix ramp of basalt spiralling up overhead, a glowing shadow-Gyroid climbing it, gold floor markers (no text).

Gyroid runs around the ring below while a glowing translucent copy of him climbs the helix above, connected by a glowing gold cord. A violet coil creature is wrapped several times around a stone pillar.

levels.title: No Way Out
levels.concept: Applications of π₁(S¹): no retraction D² → S¹, so every map D² → D² has a fixed point (Brouwer); fundamental theorem of algebra; Borsuk–Ulam in dimension 2.
levels.goal: Finally refute Count Null's World-0 claim: a ring is not a point, because its loop has winding number 1.

design.site: Brouwer's Basin — a wide round basin of stone at the Bastion's edge, rimmed by a raised ring road; Null's Retractor engine stands at its center.
design.story: Null's engineers built a Retractor to squash the whole basin onto its rim road. Gyroid finally has the tool to prove it can't work: the rim's loop winds once, but in the basin every loop shrinks — a retraction would have to unwind it. The same idea finds still points, roots and matching antipodes. And it answers World 0: a ring is not a point.
design.objective: Wreck the Retractor with a proof, then use winding to hunt still points and roots.
mechanics: The Retractor's proof-check: run the rim loop (winding 1); shrink it inside the basin; the Retractor would carry that shrinking onto the rim — the Winding Cord shows 1 can't become 0, and the engine seizes.

Arrow fields: every tile of the basin carries an arrow (a map D² → D², or a vector field). Walk the rim with the Winding Cord measuring how often the arrows turn; a nonzero count guarantees a still point inside.
Root whirlpools: a polynomial's arrows on a big circle wind n times — dive in and find its n roots.
Antipodal stations on a small sphere island: find two opposite stations reading the same two numbers.
design.math_check: No retraction D² → S¹ (π₁(D²) = 0, π₁(S¹) = ℤ); Brouwer fixed point theorem in dimension 2; the fundamental theorem of algebra via winding; Borsuk–Ulam for S²; S¹ is not contractible.

stages.name: The Retractor
stages.description: Show the rim loop can't be unwound by any retraction; the engine stalls.

stages.name: The Still Point
stages.description: Walk the rim of arrow fields; where the count isn't zero, find the tile whose arrow points nowhere.

stages.name: Roots
stages.description: A whirlpool winding three times on its rim hides three roots.

stages.name: Antipodes
stages.description: On a sphere island, find the matching pair of opposite stations.

enemies.description: New: violet drones that tug Gyroid toward the rim; two lashes.

enemies.name: Whirl spawn
enemies.description: New: spinning violet tops that scramble nearby arrows; one lash.

design.tools: Uses the Winding Cord and Loop Lash.
design.music: Low drone of the Retractor, the Bastion march breaking through triumphantly when the engine seizes.
design.visuals: A huge round stone basin with a glowing rim road, a fields of gold arrows on its tiles swirling toward a still point, a hulking violet Retractor engine at the center.

art.scene: Level 'No Way Out' at Brouwer's Basin: a vast round stone basin rimmed by a raised glowing ring road. Its tiles carry glowing gold arrows that swirl around and converge on a single still glowing point. A hulking violet machine (the Retractor) at the edge strains with chains toward the rim, sparking and seizing. Gyroid walks the rim with a gold cord.

levels.title: Push It Forward
levels.concept: Induced homomorphisms f_*; retractions induce injections; π₁(X × Y) ≅ π₁(X) × π₁(Y), so π₁(torus) ≅ ℤ².

design.site: Torus Terraces — a terraced island shaped like a torus, with one belt road around its tube and one through its hole.
design.story: Maps between places push loops forward. On the Torus Terraces, two belt roads give two independent kinds of loop — and on a torus, going around one then the other is the same as the other then the one. Loops here need two numbers.
design.objective: Use the map projectors to push loops between islands, and chart loops on the torus by two winding numbers.
mechanics: Map Projector: a machine maps one island onto another; any loop on the source projects to a loop on the target, and its winding is read off (the induced homomorphism f_*).
Retract check: when an island retracts onto a part of itself, distinct loops in the part stay distinct (the inclusion's f_* is injective).
Grid lift: on the torus, the lift lives on an endless square grid; a loop's endpoint (m, n) counts laps of each belt road.
Swap test: around-the-tube then through-the-hole slides into the other order (ab = ba on the torus).
design.math_check: Induced homomorphisms are functorial; retractions induce injections on π₁ of the subspace; π₁(X × Y) ≅ π₁(X) × π₁(Y), so π₁(T²) ≅ ℤ².

stages.name: The Projector
stages.description: Map a circle around another circle k times: winding numbers multiply by k.

stages.name: Retract Check
stages.description: An island retracts onto its ring road; loops on the road stay distinct.

stages.name: Two Roads
stages.description: Chart torus loops as (m, n) on the grid lift; tube-then-hole slides into hole-then-tube.

stages.name: Shadows
stages.description: Split torus loops into their two circle shadows and rebuild them.

enemies.name: Torus spawn
enemies.description: Two lashes — now the arena itself is a torus.

enemies.name: Projector imp
enemies.description: New: a violet imp that hijacks a projector, scrambling where loops land; one lash.

design.tools: Uses the Winding Cord; the Suspension Sling (0-5) reaches the upper terraces.
design.music: The march in a rolling 6/8, two interlocking arpeggios (one per belt road).
design.visuals: A terraced torus-shaped island of stone, two glowing gold belt roads, a translucent square grid floating overhead with Gyroid's shadow walking it.

art.scene: Level 'Push It Forward' at the Torus Terraces: a terraced island shaped like a giant torus (a ring doughnut) of stone, with one glowing gold belt road wrapping around its tube and another running around through its central hole. Above it floats a translucent square grid with a glowing shadow of Gyroid walking it. Gyroid stands on a terrace beside a brass projector machine casting a beam onto a smaller island.

levels.title: Free Word Play
levels.concept: Free products: loops in a wedge of circles are reduced words; adjacent inverses cancel; different generators don't commute.

design.site: Free-Word Forge — the beacon junction where the red district (loop a) and the violet district (loop b) meet; the Commutator's patrols march here.
design.story: In the two loop districts every lap writes a letter: a for the red loop, b for the violet, and inverses for laps run backwards. Adjacent opposites cancel; nothing else does. The Commutator's patrols march a, b, a⁻¹, b⁻¹ — a word that never cancels. Gyroid forges the Van Kampen Clasp to work with words.
design.objective: Reduce loop words, learn why order matters, and intercept the Commutator's patrol.
mechanics: Word tape: each lap of a district prints a letter (a, a⁻¹, b, b⁻¹) on the tape over Gyroid's head.
Cancel: an adjacent pair like a a⁻¹ snaps off the tape (reduction).
Reduced words are unique: two different reduced words are different loops (proved in 1-8 with a cover).
Van Kampen Clasp (new): join word tapes at the beacon; keeps generator order visible as colored beads.
Ribbon patrols walk a fixed word; they dissolve only when lashed in the reverse order of their word.
design.math_check: π₁(S¹ ∨ S¹) is the free group on a, b: reduced words, unique normal form, ab ≠ ba.

stages.name: Laps Are Letters
stages.description: Run laps and watch the tape.

stages.name: Cancel
stages.description: Reduce long patrol words to their shortest form.

stages.name: Order Matters
stages.description: Walk a then b, and b then a: no slide turns one into the other. Emmy promises a proof at the Viaduct.

stages.name: The Patrol
stages.description: Intercept a patrol walking a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹; its word doesn't reduce, so its guard can't be talked down — lash it in reverse order.

enemies.name: Ribbon patrol
enemies.description: New: the Commutator's guards; each walks a word and dissolves only when lashed in reverse word order.

enemies.name: Torus spawn
enemies.description: Two lashes.

design.tools: Unlocks the Van Kampen Clasp (van_kampen_clasp).
design.music: A two-voice canon (red voice, violet voice) that never quite lines up — order matters.
design.visuals: Red-lantern and violet-lantern ring districts meeting at the amber beacon, a floating tape of colored beads over Gyroid, ribbon guards in tall pauldrons marching.

art.scene: Level 'Free Word Play' at the Free-Word Forge: two ring-shaped stone districts meet at an amber beacon, one lined with red lanterns and one with violet-steel lanterns. A floating ribbon of colored beads (red and violet) hovers over Gyroid like a tape. Tall violet guards with big asymmetrical loop-shaped pauldrons march in a line along the causeways, trailing ribbons.

levels.title: Glue Job
levels.concept: Van Kampen's theorem; attaching a 2-cell kills its boundary word: π₁(torus) = ⟨a, b | aba⁻¹b⁻¹⟩, π₁(RP²) = ℤ₂, surfaces.

design.site: Glue Works — a workshop where disks are pressed onto loop districts.
design.story: Glue a disk onto a loop and that loop can slide across the disk and vanish. Glue a disk along a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹ and the figure-eight becomes a torus — the Commutator's favorite word dies. Glue along a a and walking the loop twice means nothing, but once still counts.
design.objective: Attach disks to change which words survive, and compute groups of glued places.
mechanics: Cell-Smith + Clasp: walk a word along the districts; the press glues a disk onto exactly that loop.
After gluing, the word on the disk's edge slides across the disk to nothing — it becomes a relation.
Van Kampen: an island made of two overlapping pieces gets its words from both pieces, with the shared part's words identified.
design.math_check: Van Kampen's theorem; attaching a 2-cell along a loop adds that word as a relation: ⟨a, b | aba⁻¹b⁻¹⟩ = ℤ² for the torus, ⟨a | a²⟩ = ℤ₂ for RP², trivial for the sphere.

stages.name: Glue a Disk
stages.description: A disk on a circle: its loop vanishes (the disk is contractible).

stages.name: The Torus
stages.description: Glue along a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹: now a then b slides into b then a.

stages.name: Half Turn
stages.description: Glue along a a: walking the loop twice slides away; once doesn't — RP², two classes.

stages.name: Two Pieces
stages.description: Compute an island's group from two overlapping pieces (Van Kampen).

enemies.name: Unglue
enemies.description: From 0-4: tears disks off — re-glue before the relation is lost.

enemies.name: Ribbon patrol
enemies.description: Its word may die on a glued district — then it can be dissolved with a single lash.

design.tools: Uses the Cell-Smith and the Van Kampen Clasp.
design.music: Forge percussion from World 0 under the Bastion march — the two worlds' tools working together.
design.visuals: A workshop over the loop districts: presses lowering translucent gold disks onto glowing loops, a square sheet folding into a torus.

art.scene: Level 'Glue Job' in the Glue Works: an industrial stone workshop above ring causeways; great presses lower translucent glowing gold disks onto glowing loop roads. In the center, a flat glowing square sheet with arrow-marked edges folds into a torus. Gyroid wears a brass-and-indigo gauntlet and holds a copper clasp joining red and violet cords.

levels.title: Under Cover
levels.concept: Covering spaces; unique path and homotopy lifting; a loop's class lies in p_*π₁ exactly when its lift closes; sheets = index.

design.site: Sheetwater Viaduct — a three-layer viaduct of glass sheets above a figure-eight causeway; each sheet repeats the causeway with labeled ports.
design.story: Above the figure-eight, three glass sheets copy it, and every step below moves a lift along the matching edge above. A loop below can end on a different sheet above — its lift doesn't close. With the Sheet Compass, Gyroid finally proves what 1-6 only suspected: a then b and b then a are different loops.
design.objective: Build covers that obey the local rules, lift routes to reach sheets, and use closed lifts to tell loops apart.
mechanics: Sheet Compass (new): shows which sheet the lift is on; every step in the base moves the lift along the matching labeled edge.
Local rule: at every vertex of a cover, exactly one incoming and one outgoing edge of each label.
A base loop's lift closes exactly when the loop belongs to the cover's subgroup; the number of sheets is its index.
Proof by cover: find a cover where a b lifts to a closed loop and b a doesn't — so they can't be the same loop.
design.math_check: Covering spaces: unique path and homotopy lifting; p_* is injective; a loop's class is in p_*π₁ iff its lift closes; sheets = index; ab ≠ ba in F₂.

stages.name: Two Floors
stages.description: A two-sheet cover of a circle: a single lap opens the lift; two laps close it.

stages.name: Build a Cover
stages.description: Wire a three-sheet cover of the figure-eight obeying the local rule.

stages.name: Rescue on Sheet Two
stages.description: Lift a given route to reach Emmy, trapped on sheet two.

stages.name: Order, Proved
stages.description: Build a cover where a b closes and b a doesn't.

enemies.name: Liftling
enemies.description: New: violet sprites that live on one sheet; only Gyroid's lift on that sheet can lash them.

enemies.name: Ribbon patrol
enemies.description: Patrols the base causeway.

design.tools: Unlocks the Sheet Compass (sheet_compass).
design.music: Sheetwater theme: three layered pads, one per sheet, entering and dropping as the lift changes sheets; glassy harp arpeggios.
design.visuals: Three stacked translucent glass sheets over a figure-eight causeway, glowing ports at each vertex, Gyroid below and a luminous lift-Gyroid above.

art.scene: Level 'Under Cover' at the Sheetwater Viaduct: three stacked translucent glass sheets float one above another over a figure-eight stone causeway on the sea; each sheet repeats the causeway's shape, with glowing ports at the junctions. Gyroid walks the causeway below while a luminous translucent copy of him walks the second glass sheet above. Emmy Boundary stands trapped on a higher sheet, waving.

levels.title: Sheet Music
levels.concept: Classification: connected covers ↔ subgroups of π₁ (up to conjugacy); covers of S¹ ∨ S¹ as labeled graphs; universal covers (tree, plane).

design.site: Sheet Stacks — towers of glass sheets of every size, built to order.
design.story: Every connected cover of the figure-eight matches a choice of which loops should close — a subgroup. The Stacks build covers to order, including the endless one where no loop closes but the trivial one: a tree. Over a torus, the endless cover is a plane.
design.objective: Build covers to order, see how moving the start changes the order, and walk the universal covers.
mechanics: Orders: a request lists loops that must close and loops that must not; build the cover.
Moving the start vertex changes the subgroup to a conjugate one.
The endless tree: a four-way branching viaduct over the figure-eight; each reduced word ends at a different vertex.
The plane over the torus: an endless grid; loops (m, n) end at lattice points.
design.math_check: Classification of covering spaces: connected covers ↔ conjugacy classes of subgroups of π₁; the universal cover (a tree for S¹ ∨ S¹, the plane for T²).

stages.name: To Order
stages.description: Request: a a closes, a doesn't — build a two-sheet cover.

stages.name: Moving the Start
stages.description: Same cover, different start: a conjugate order.

stages.name: The Endless Tree
stages.description: Walk the universal cover: every reduced word ends somewhere new.

stages.name: Plane over Torus
stages.description: Lift torus loops to the endless grid and read their (m, n).

enemies.name: Liftling
enemies.description: Live on specific sheets.

enemies.name: Stack sentinel
enemies.description: New: guards a cover's start vertex and swaps it when struck wrong; two lashes.

design.tools: Uses the Sheet Compass and Van Kampen Clasp.
design.music: Sheetwater theme in canon at different octaves — one voice per sheet.
design.visuals: Towers of stacked glass sheets of varying heights, an infinitely branching glowing tree viaduct receding into fog, an endless grid plane over a small torus island.

art.scene: Level 'Sheet Music' at the Sheet Stacks: towers of stacked glass sheets of different heights; in the background an endlessly branching glowing gold tree-shaped viaduct recedes into fog, and beside it an endless glowing square grid plane floats over a small torus island. Gyroid stands on a glass sheet holding a glowing compass.

levels.title: Deck the Halls
levels.concept: Deck transformations and group actions; normal covers; Sⁿ → RPⁿ.

design.site: Deck Halls — vaulted halls where whole sheets of a cover can be shifted at once.
design.story: Some covers are perfectly symmetric: shift every sheet at once and nothing changes. These deck shifts form a group. A sphere hall where opposite points are the same room is a two-sheet cover of the projective plane.
design.objective: Find the deck shifts of covers, tell symmetric (normal) covers from lopsided ones, and walk the antipodal hall.
mechanics: Deck Shift: rotate or swap all sheets of a cover at once; allowed only if every labeled edge still matches.
Normal covers: a shift can carry any sheet to any other over a point.
Quotients: a cover built as a space divided by a free group action.
Antipodal Hall: a sphere where opposite doors open into the same room; a loop below can lift to a path between opposite points.
design.math_check: Deck transformations, normal covers (deck group transitive on fibers), covering spaces from free properly discontinuous actions, S² → RP².

stages.name: Shift the Deck
stages.description: A three-sheet cyclic cover: rotating the sheets changes nothing.

stages.name: Lopsided
stages.description: A cover with no shift between some sheets: not normal.

stages.name: Divide by a Group
stages.description: Build a cover as a quotient of a free action.

stages.name: The Antipodal Hall
stages.description: Walk S² over RP²: find the loop that lifts to a path between opposite doors.

enemies.name: Deck guard
enemies.description: New: violet guards copied on every sheet; lash all copies with one well-chosen deck shift.

enemies.name: Liftling
enemies.description: Sheet-bound.

design.tools: Uses the Sheet Compass.
design.music: A rotating round: the same phrase passed between three voices (one per sheet) in cycle.
design.visuals: Vaulted glass halls with stacked floors shifting in unison, a spherical hall with paired opposite doors glowing gold.

art.scene: Level 'Deck the Halls' in the Deck Halls: vaulted halls of glass with stacked floors rotating in unison like a carousel, and a great spherical hall with pairs of glowing gold doors placed exactly opposite each other. Gyroid stands at the center of the sphere hall. Violet guards appear copied identically on every floor.

levels.title: Free Agents
levels.concept: Bonus: graphs and free groups — subgroups of free groups are free, via covers of graphs.

design.site: Free Agents' Grove — a quiet grove of glass-sheet trees off the Viaduct.
design.story: A cover of a graph is a graph. Fell its spanning tree (0-6) and count petals: every subgroup of a free group is free, and Gyroid can count its generators.
design.objective: Take covers of the figure-eight, collapse their trees, and count petals.
mechanics: Pick a cover; mark and fell a spanning tree with the Spool (0-6).
Count petals: an n-sheet cover of the figure-eight leaves n + 1 petals.
design.math_check: Subgroups of free groups are free (Nielsen–Schreier via covers); an index-n subgroup of F₂ has rank n + 1 (χ multiplies by n).

stages.name: Fell a Cover
stages.description: A two-sheet cover collapses to three petals.

stages.name: Count
stages.description: Predict petals from sheets before felling.

enemies.name: Loop-biter
enemies.description: From 0-6: protect the petals.

design.music: Woodwind theme from the Timber Yard, transposed into the Bastion key.
design.visuals: Glass-sheet trees whose branches are covering graphs, amber trees folding into bouquets.

art.scene: Bonus level 'Free Agents' in a quiet grove: glass trees whose branches form glowing graph networks; amber highlighted branches fold inward, leaving a bouquet of glowing loops around a single node. Gyroid sits beneath one tree with a thick gold ring.

levels.title: One Group to Rule
levels.concept: Bonus: K(G,1) spaces and graphs of groups.

design.site: One-Group Tower — a tower whose every floor is a space with a contractible universal cover.
design.story: Some places are completely described by their loops: everything above dimension one is filled. These are K(G,1) spaces, and the tower collects them.
design.objective: Recognize spaces whose universal cover is contractible.
mechanics: Walk each floor's universal cover (tree, plane): if it shrinks to a point, the floor is a K(G,1).
Graphs of groups: glue floors along shared loops.
design.math_check: K(G,1) spaces: contractible universal cover; graphs are K(F,1); the torus is K(ℤ²,1).

stages.name: Contractible Above
stages.description: The endless tree and the endless plane both shrink.

stages.name: Stacked Floors
stages.description: Glue floors along loops and keep the property.

enemies.name: None
enemies.description: A contemplative bonus.

design.music: Music-box variation of the Sheetwater theme.
design.visuals: A tall tower of glass floors, each showing a tree or plane receding into fog.

art.scene: Bonus level 'One Group to Rule': a tall tower of glass floors at night; through each floor you see an endless branching tree or an endless grid plane receding into fog. Gyroid climbs a spiral stair inside.

castle.title: The Commutator's Keep
castle.outcome: The Commutator's patrol aba⁻¹b⁻¹ is nontrivial in the figure-eight (catch it with a cover where its lift doesn't close) but dies on the torus (the 2-cell). Null retreats to the sphere, where loops are blind.

design.site: The Commutator's Keep — a fortress of two interlocking loop towers, its door on the second sheet of the Viaduct.
design.story: Null's route marshal holds the Keep, his ribbon patrols marching a, b, a⁻¹, b⁻¹ forever. Gyroid proves the patrol can't be undone in the figure-eight — then Emmy glues a disk and turns the arena into a torus, where the patrol's word dies. The Commutator falls back; Null retreats to a sphere, where every loop shrinks.
design.objective: Defeat the Commutator by breaking the meaning of his patrol word.

phases.name: The patrol
phases.description: In a figure-eight arena the Commutator dashes his word a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹. Build a cover on the arena where his lift doesn't close; lash him on the sheet where it ends. Tests 1-6 and 1-8.

phases.name: Ribbon storm
phases.description: He splits into ribbon copies on several sheets; one deck shift lines them up for a single lash. Tests 1-9 and 1-10.

design.movie: castle-1-intro “The Commutator's Keep” and castle-1-outro “Loops Go Blind”.

Inside, a figure-eight shaped arena floor with three translucent glass sheets stacked above it. worlds.title: Chain Delta
worlds.theme: Wetlands of oriented triangles where boundaries cancel and missing centers survive.

null_claim.claim: The torus and S¹ ∨ S¹ ∨ S² are the same place.

levels.title: Tile and Error
levels.concept: Δ-complexes: glue ordered simplices; torus, Klein bottle, RP² from two triangles.

design.site: Tile Yard — the delta's edge, where triangle platforms are stacked, labeled with arrows and glued together.
design.story: Chain Delta is built from triangles whose edges carry arrows. Before Gyroid can count holes of every dimension he must learn how places are built from ordered triangles: two triangles make a torus, a Klein bottle or a projective plane, depending only on how their arrows are matched.
design.objective: Assemble surfaces from triangles by matching arrowed edges.
mechanics: Triangle crane: pick triangles up and lower them so their edges meet; edges glue only if arrows agree (vertices are ordered, and every edge runs from lower to higher vertex).
Glue preview: after gluing, the crane shows the resulting surface floating above the yard.
Vertex count: identified corners fuse into one; the yard tallies vertices, edges and triangles (χ, from 0-4).
design.math_check: Δ-complexes: simplices with ordered vertices, faces glued by order-preserving identifications; the torus, Klein bottle and RP² each from two triangles (Hatcher pp. 102–104).

stages.name: Two Triangles
stages.description: Glue two triangles along one edge into a square.

stages.name: The Torus
stages.description: Glue the square's opposite edges with matching arrows: a torus — one vertex, three edges, two triangles.

stages.name: Flip an Arrow
stages.description: Same square, one pair reversed: a Klein bottle. Both pairs crossed: a projective plane.

stages.name: Wrong Order
stages.description: Repair Null's sabotaged yard, where arrows were relabeled so that gluings no longer respect vertex order.

enemies.name: Flipper
enemies.description: New: a violet frog that hops onto an edge and reverses its arrow; one lash.

enemies.name: Unglue
enemies.description: From 0-4: tears freshly glued edges.

design.tools: Uses the Cell-Smith (gluing) and the Lash.
design.music: Chain Delta theme: a hushed 84 bpm piece in E minor, marimba arpeggios over a low drone, water drips on the offbeat — first statement.
design.visuals: Dusk wetland, floating stone triangle platforms with glowing amber arrows on their edges, a brass crane, a translucent torus forming overhead.

art.scene: Level 'Tile and Error' in the Tile Yard: a dusk wetland where floating stone triangle platforms with glowing amber arrows along their edges are stacked and moved by a brass crane. Two triangles glued into a square hang from the crane; above them a translucent glowing torus forms. Gyroid guides the crane. A small violet frog sits on an edge.

levels.title: Boundary Issues
levels.concept: Simplicial chains, ∂∂ = 0, cycles modulo boundaries.

design.site: Cancel Marsh — a marsh of tiled triangles, some fused into larger plazas.
design.story: Emmy forges the Boundary Blade: cut anything along its edge, with arrows, and shared interior edges cancel. Cut a boundary again and nothing is left — every time. A loop that is not the edge of anything is a cycle that survives: a hole.
design.objective: Use the Boundary Blade to find cycles, boundaries, and the holes left between them.
mechanics: Boundary Blade (new): strike a tile or a patch of tiles; its boundary lights as an arrowed loop, interior shared edges cancelling (one arrow each way).
Strike again: the boundary of a boundary is always empty — the blade passes through without a mark (∂∂ = 0).
Cycles: chains with no boundary. Boundaries: cycles that are edges of something. Holes: cycles that are not boundaries.
Hole meter: the meter counts surviving cycle classes in each dimension (cycles modulo boundaries).
design.math_check: Simplicial chains Cₙ, ∂ with alternating signs, ∂∂ = 0, Hₙ = ker ∂ₙ / im ∂ₙ₊₁ (Hatcher pp. 104–108).

stages.name: First Cut
stages.description: Strike one triangle: three arrowed edges light.

stages.name: Shared Edges
stages.description: Strike a plaza of triangles: the interior edges cancel and only the outer boundary remains.

stages.name: Nothing Left
stages.description: Strike the boundary itself: nothing — every vertex appears once with + and once with −.

stages.name: The Missing Tile
stages.description: A ring of tiles around a missing one: its inner loop is a cycle but not a boundary. Count H₁.

enemies.name: Flipper
enemies.description: Reverses arrows so edges stop cancelling.

enemies.name: Bog spawn
enemies.description: New: a violet blob that fills in missing tiles, hiding holes; two lashes (it is 2-dimensional).

design.tools: Unlocks the Boundary Blade (boundary_blade).
design.music: Chain Delta theme with a soft bell for every cancelling edge pair.
design.visuals: A marsh of triangle tiles; a glowing gold blade leaving arrowed outlines; pairs of opposite arrows dissolving into sparks; a dark gap where one tile is missing.

art.scene: Level 'Boundary Issues' in Cancel Marsh: a marsh of stone triangle tiles over dark water. Gyroid swings a glowing gold blade of light; it leaves a glowing arrowed outline around a plaza of triangles, with sparks where interior opposite arrows cancel. In the middle of a ring of tiles, one tile is missing, leaving a dark gap. A violet blob oozes toward the gap.

levels.title: Any Simplex Will Do
levels.concept: Singular homology and homotopy invariance.

design.site: Singular Shallows — misty shallows where triangles can be bent, crumpled and collapsed into any shape.
design.story: Real places don't come with tidy triangles. In the Shallows, any map of a triangle counts — even crumpled ones. Homology built from all of them gives the same answer as the tidy count, and places that deform into each other (0-3) have the same homology.
design.objective: Measure holes with crumpled triangles, and see that deforming a place never changes its homology.
mechanics: Singular stamps: stamp a triangle into the shallows along any map — stretched, folded or squashed to a line.
The Boundary Blade works on stamps exactly as on tiles.
Deform test: slide a place with the Tide Glass (0-2) or retract it (0-1); the hole meter doesn't change.
Path components: the meter's H₀ counts separate pieces.
design.math_check: Singular homology; H₀ counts path components; homotopy-equivalent spaces have isomorphic homology; it agrees with simplicial homology on Δ-complexes (Hatcher pp. 108–113; the agreement is proved on p. 128).

stages.name: Any Triangle
stages.description: Stamp crumpled triangles; the blade still cuts their edges.

stages.name: Pieces
stages.description: Count separate islands with H₀.

stages.name: Bend, Don't Change
stages.description: Retract a fat annulus to its core circle: the meter stays at one 1-dimensional hole.

stages.name: Same Shape, Same Count
stages.description: Bring back the Mirror Couriers (0-3): equivalent places read identically on every meter.

enemies.name: Mirror spawn
enemies.description: From 0-3: copies a place in a lumpier shape.

enemies.name: Crumpler
enemies.description: New: a violet wad that stamps degenerate triangles to confuse the meter; one lash.

design.tools: Uses the Boundary Blade, Tide Glass and Spool.
design.music: Chain Delta theme slowed and blurred with reverb, like hearing it through fog.
design.visuals: Misty shallows; gold triangles crumpled, folded and stretched like cloth; the meter floating as a glowing abacus (no numerals).

art.scene: Level 'Any Simplex Will Do' in the Singular Shallows: misty shallow water; glowing gold triangles are stretched, folded and crumpled like cloth over the water. A glowing abacus floats in the air. Gyroid stamps a triangle into the shallows. A violet crumpled wad creature lurks.

levels.title: Chase Scene
levels.concept: Exact sequences, long exact sequence of a pair, diagram chasing.

design.site: Chase Channels — canals arranged in long rows of locks, each lock feeding the next.
design.story: Water flows from lock to lock; whatever leaves one is exactly what the next one drains — an exact sequence. Gyroid learns to chase a drop of water through the grid, and to read a place's homology from a pair: the place and a part of it.
design.objective: Chase elements through lock diagrams and use the long exact sequence of a pair.
mechanics: Locks are groups; sluices are maps. A row is exact where the water entering a lock is exactly what the next sluice discards.
Diagram chase: carry a drop down, across and back up the grid; each move must follow a sluice or reverse one where exactness allows.
The pair sequence: for a place X and a part A, locks for A, X and (X, A) link into one long chain, joined by the connecting sluice ∂.
Relative cycles: chains in X whose edge lies in A.
design.math_check: Exact sequences, short exact sequences of chain complexes give long exact sequences, the long exact sequence of a pair, diagram chasing, the five lemma (Hatcher pp. 113–118).

stages.name: Exact Locks
stages.description: Check exactness lock by lock.

stages.name: The Chase
stages.description: Chase a drop to build the connecting sluice ∂.

stages.name: A Place and a Part
stages.description: Compute the homology of a disk relative to its rim from the pair sequence.

stages.name: Five Locks
stages.description: Two rows joined by sluices; four are known to be perfect transfers: prove the middle one is too.

enemies.name: Leak sprite
enemies.description: New: punctures locks so water escapes and exactness breaks; seal the leak, then lash.

enemies.name: Flipper
enemies.description: Reverses sluices.

design.tools: Uses the Boundary Blade.
design.music: A steady 96 bpm canal-boat groove; each lock adds an instrument as the chase passes through it.
design.visuals: Rows of stone canal locks with glowing amber water, sluice gates in grids, a single gold drop tracing a path across the grid.
